claim: External application of MTSEA was without discernible effect on rP2X2–3 T.
source: Similar to MTSET, the external application of MTSEA was without discernible effect on rP2X2–3 T (Figure 4A, B, E, F).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results and supported by Figure 4A, B, E, F.

claim: External application of MTSEA in the presence of ATP produced robust and irreversible inhibition of ATP-activated current for the E17C rP2X2–3 T channel.
source: Also similar to MTSET, external application of MTSEA in the presence of ATP produced robust and irreversible inhibition of ATP-activated current for the E17C rP2X2–3 T channel (Figure 4C, D and E), suggesting that external MTSEA can access E17 through the ion permeation pathway.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results and supported by Figure 4C, D and E.

claim: External MTSEA can access E17 through the ion permeation pathway.
source: Also similar to MTSET, external application of MTSEA in the presence of ATP produced robust and irreversible inhibition of ATP-activated current for the E17C rP2X2–3 T channel (Figure 4C, D and E), suggesting that external MTSEA can access E17 through the ion permeation pathway.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results as an inference from the data.

claim: External application of MTSEA in the absence of ATP produced discernible inhibition of currents activated by subsequent application of ATP for E17C rP2X2–3 T.
source: However, in contrast to MTSET, external application of MTSEA in the absence of ATP produced discernible inhibition of currents activated by subsequent application of ATP (Figure 4D and F).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results and supported by Figure 4D and F.

claim: External MTSEA can access E17C through the ion permeation pathway when the channel is open, or cross the membrane and react with E17C from the intracellular side when the channel is closed.
source: Inhibition produced by external application of MTSEA in the absence of ATP prevented subsequent inhibition by external application of MTSEA in the presence of ATP (Figure 4D and F), suggesting that external MTSEA can access E17C through the ion permeation pathway when the channel is open, or cross the membrane and react with E17C from the intracellular side when the channel is closed.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results as an inference from the data.

claim: MTSET modified E17C with a rate of 3.7 × 10² M⁻¹s⁻¹.
source: The time courses for MTS modification in the presence of ATP could be reasonably well fit by a single exponential function (Figure 5A and B), from which we calculate that MTSET modified E17C with a rate of 3.7 × 102 M–1s–1, while the smaller MTSEA modified that position with a rate of 2.6 × 103 M–1s–1 (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results and supported by Figure 5A, B, and D.

claim: MTSEA modified E17C with a rate of 2.6 × 10³ M⁻¹s⁻¹.
source: The time courses for MTS modification in the presence of ATP could be reasonably well fit by a single exponential function (Figure 5A and B), from which we calculate that MTSET modified E17C with a rate of 3.7 × 102 M–1s–1, while the smaller MTSEA modified that position with a rate of 2.6 × 103 M–1s–1 (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results and supported by Figure 5A, B, and D.

claim: The modification rate for externally applied MTSET at E17C is only incrementally slower than the deepest position in the transmembrane region.
source: From previous MTSET modification rates obtained in the presence of ATP for multiple positions within the TM2 helix, we can appreciate that rates of modification diminish as Cys residues are introduced deeper into the pore (Figure 5D). Notably, the modification rate for externally applied MTSET at E17C is only incrementally slower than the deepest position in the transmembrane region when applying the reagent to the external solution (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results and supported by Figure 5D.

claim: The relatively rapid rates of modification suggest that E17C is positioned in a high dielectric environment that is favorable for modification.
source: Given that the reagents must traverse the entire TM pore to react with E17C, these relatively rapid rates of modification suggest that E17C is positioned in a high dielectric environment that is favorable for modification.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results as an inference from the data.

claim: The most intracellular end of the lateral fenestrations, where E17 is located, resides in an aqueous environment.
source: Although, lipid molecules likely occupy the upper regions of the lateral fenestrations, it seems unavoidable that the most intracellular end of the lateral fenestrations, where E17 is located, resides in an aqueous environment.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results as an inference from the data.

claim: E17 lines the intracellular end of the ion permeation pathway.
source: From these experiments examining the modification of E17C within the lateral fenestrations, we conclude that this residue lines the intracellular end of the ion permeation pathway.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results as a conclusion from the data.

claim: For wild-type rP2X2 receptor channels, Vrev was measured near 0 mV with symmetric solutions and shifted to around –32 mV upon switching to external solution containing 40 mM NaCl.
source: For wild-type rP2X2 receptor channels, we measured Vrev with symmetric solutions near 0 mV and upon switching to the external containing 40 mM NaCl observed that Vrev shifted to around –32 mV (Figure 6A and G), from which we calculate a pNa+:pCl- of 20:1 using the Goldman-Hodgkin-Katz equation (see Materials and methods), indicative of a strong preference for cations over anions.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results and supported by Figure 6A and G.

claim: Wild-type rP2X2 has a pNa+:pCl- of 20:1.
source: For wild-type rP2X2 receptor channels, we measured Vrev with symmetric solutions near 0 mV and upon switching to the external containing 40 mM NaCl observed that Vrev shifted to around –32 mV (Figure 6A and G), from which we calculate a pNa+:pCl- of 20:1 using the Goldman-Hodgkin-Katz equation (see Materials and methods), indicative of a strong preference for cations over anions.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results and supported by Figure 6A and G.

claim: Wild-type rP2X2 exhibits a strong preference for cations over anions.
source: For wild-type rP2X2 receptor channels, we measured Vrev with symmetric solutions near 0 mV and upon switching to the external containing 40 mM NaCl observed that Vrev shifted to around –32 mV (Figure 6A and G), from which we calculate a pNa+:pCl- of 20:1 using the Goldman-Hodgkin-Katz equation (see Materials and methods), indicative of a strong preference for cations over anions.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results and supported by Figure 6A and G.

claim: rP2X2 is inwardly rectifying.
source: Considering that rP2X2 is inwardly rectifying and thus passes outward currents less favorably than inward currents (Zhou and Hume, 1998; Fujiwara and Kubo, 2004; George et al., 2019), we also used voltage step protocols and measured the initial tail current on stepping from –60 mV to more positive voltages, enabling the measurement of relatively linear instantaneous I-V relations and an independent determination of Vrev (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results and supported by citations.

claim: The E17K mutation did not appreciably alter the concentration-dependence for activation of the channel by ATP.
source: The E17K mutation did not appreciably alter the concentration-dependence for activation of the channel by ATP (Figure 6H), suggesting that the mutation does not perturb gating.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results and supported by Figure 6H.

claim: The E17K mutation does not perturb gating of rP2X2.
source: The E17K mutation did not appreciably alter the concentration-dependence for activation of the channel by ATP (Figure 6H), suggesting that the mutation does not perturb gating.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results as an inference from the data.

claim: The E17K mutation altered the shift in Vrev produced by lowering external NaCl concentration, shifting Vrev to between –22 mV and –25 mV.
source: However, the E17K mutation did alter the shift in Vrev produced by lowering external NaCl concentration, shifting Vrev to between –22 mV and –25 mV depending on whether we used ramp or step protocols, and whether ions were substituted with sucrose or glucose (Figure 6D–G).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results and supported by Figure 6D–G.

claim: The E17K mutation diminished pNa+:pCl- to 10:1 from 20:1 measured for the wild-type rP2X2 receptor.
source: If we calculate the relative permeability of cations to anions, the E17K diminished pNa+:pCl- to 10:1 from 20:1 measured for the wild-type receptor.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results and supported by experimental data.

claim: E17 is not the sole determinant of cation selectivity in P2X2 receptor channels.
source: Although these results establish that E17 is not the sole determinant of cation selectivity in P2X2 receptor channels, mutation of this residue detectably alters cation selectivity, consistent with this residue residing within the ion permeation pathway on the intracellular side of the membrane.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results as a conclusion from the data.

claim: Mutation of E17 detectably alters cation selectivity in P2X2 receptor channels.
source: Although these results establish that E17 is not the sole determinant of cation selectivity in P2X2 receptor channels, mutation of this residue detectably alters cation selectivity, consistent with this residue residing within the ion permeation pathway on the intracellular side of the membrane.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results as a conclusion from the data.

claim: E17 resides within the ion permeation pathway on the intracellular side of the membrane.
source: Although these results establish that E17 is not the sole determinant of cation selectivity in P2X2 receptor channels, mutation of this residue detectably alters cation selectivity, consistent with this residue residing within the ion permeation pathway on the intracellular side of the membrane.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results as an inference from the data.

claim: Expression of the mouse P2X5 clone produced the largest ATP-activated currents in standard extracellular solution lacking divalent cations.
source: We initially expressed P2X5 receptor channels from rat and mouse but observed that expression of the mouse clone produced the largest ATP-activated currents in our standard extracellular solution lacking divalent cations (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results and supported by experimental data.

claim: A robust yet variable sensitization phenomenon was observed whereby ATP-activated currents in cells expressing mP2X5 increased in amplitude over the time course of several minutes.
source: We also observed a robust yet variable sensitization phenomenon whereby ATP-activated currents in cells expressing mP2X5 increased in amplitude over the time course of several minutes (Figure 7A and B).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results and supported by Figure 7A and B.

claim: mP2X5 has a relatively high affinity for ATP in the absence of divalent ions, roughly two orders of magnitude higher than wild-type rP2X2.
source: Examination of the concentration-dependence for activation of mP2X5 revealed a relatively high affinity for ATP in the absence of divalent ions, roughly two orders of magnitude higher than wild-type rP2X2 (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results and supported by Figure 7C.

claim: Decreasing the concentration of external NaCl did not shift Vrev towards negative voltages for mP2X5, but instead produced a slight positive shift in Vrev by a few mV.
source: Remarkably, decreasing the concentration of external NaCl did not shift Vrev towards negative voltages, as we observed for rP2X2, but instead produced a slight positive shift in Vrev by a few mV (Figure 8A and D).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results and supported by Figure 8A and D.

claim: mP2X5 has a slight preference for anions over cations, with a relative permeability of pNa+:pCl- of 0.8.
source: From these shifts in Vrev, we calculate that mP2X5 has a slight preference for anions over cations, with a relative permeability of pNa+:pCl- of 0.8.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results and supported by experimental data.

claim: These findings confirm earlier reports that P2X5 receptor channels have a much higher Cl- permeability compared to other subtypes of P2X receptor channels.
source: These findings confirm earlier reports that P2X5 receptor channels have a much higher Cl- permeability compared to other subtypes of P2X receptor channels (Ruppelt et al., 2001; Bo et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results and supported by citations.

claim: Neither K17E nor K17D mutations in mP2X5 appreciably altered the concentration-dependence for activation by external ATP.
source: To explore whether K17 is a determinant of the ion selectivity of mP2X5 receptor channel, we mutated this position to either Glu or Asp. Neither mutation appreciably altered the concentration-dependence for activation of mP2X5 by external ATP (Figure 7C), suggesting that as for rP2X2, mutations at this position within the lateral fenestrations do not appreciably alter gating.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results and supported by Figure 7C.

claim: Mutations at position 17 within the lateral fenestrations do not appreciably alter gating in mP2X5.
source: To explore whether K17 is a determinant of the ion selectivity of mP2X5 receptor channel, we mutated this position to either Glu or Asp. Neither mutation appreciably altered the concentration-dependence for activation of mP2X5 by external ATP (Figure 7C), suggesting that as for rP2X2, mutations at this position within the lateral fenestrations do not appreciably alter gating.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results as an inference from the data.

claim: For both K17E and K17D mutants of mP2X5, lowering the external NaCl concentration produced dramatic shifts of Vrev to voltages between –32 mV and –35 mV.
source: We then proceeded to measure shifts in Vrev upon switching external solutions from 140 mM NaCl to 40 mM NaCl, and strikingly observed that for both mutants, lowering the external NaCl concentration produced dramatic shifts of Vrev to voltages between –32 mV and –35 mV (Figure 8B–D), similar to what we observed for wild-type rP2X2 receptor channels (Figure 6A–C and G).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results and supported by Figure 8B–D.

claim: K17E and K17D mutants of mP2X5 are strongly cation-selective, with pNa+:pCl- of around 20:1.
source: From these shifts in Vrev, we calculate that K17E and K17D mutants are strongly cation-selective, with pNa+:pCl- of around 20:1, indistinguishable from what we measured for wild-type rP2X2 receptor channels.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results and supported by experimental data.

claim: K17 is a critical determinant of the unusual anion permeability of mP2X5 receptor channels.
source: These findings indicate that K17 is a critical determinant of the unusual anion permeability of mP2X5 receptor channels.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results as a conclusion from the data.

claim: The lateral fenestrations observed in recent structures of P2X3 and P2X7 receptor channels contribute to the intracellular end of the ion permeation pathway.
source: Collectively, our results support the idea that the lateral fenestrations observed in recent structures of P2X3 and P2X7 receptor channels contribute to the intracellular end of the ion permeation pathway.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results as a conclusion from the data.

claim: The lateral fenestrations were observed for detergent-solubilized proteins.
source: One enigmatic feature of the lateral fenestrations is that they were observed for detergent-solubilized proteins, and one might expect that they would be partially or completely buried within the lipid bilayer when the protein resides in a membrane environment, in agreement with many residues at the edges of the lateral fenestrations having hydrophobic side chains (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion.

claim: An acidic residue Glu at the intracellular edge of the lateral fenestrations is conserved in P2X receptors thought to be cation-selective.
source: However, an acidic residue Glu at the intracellular edge of the lateral fenestrations is conserved in P2X receptors thought to be cation-selective but is substituted with the basic residue Lys in P2X5 (Figure 1), the one subtype of P2X receptor reported to also be anion permeable.
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion and supported by Figure 1.

claim: The acidic residue Glu at the intracellular edge of the lateral fenestrations is substituted with the basic residue Lys in P2X5.
source: However, an acidic residue Glu at the intracellular edge of the lateral fenestrations is conserved in P2X receptors thought to be cation-selective but is substituted with the basic residue Lys in P2X5 (Figure 1), the one subtype of P2X receptor reported to also be anion permeable.
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion and supported by Figure 1.

claim: The membrane-permeant MTSEA could react with E17C either when the channel was opened by external ATP, or when applied in the closed state in the absence of ATP.
source: In contrast, the membrane-permeant MTSEA could react with E17C either when the channel was opened by external ATP, or when applied in the closed state in the absence of ATP (Figure 4), indicating that E17C is accessible from both sides of the membrane.
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion and supported by Figure 4.

claim: E17C is accessible from both sides of the membrane.
source: In contrast, the membrane-permeant MTSEA could react with E17C either when the channel was opened by external ATP, or when applied in the closed state in the absence of ATP (Figure 4), indicating that E17C is accessible from both sides of the membrane.
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion and supported by Figure 4.

claim: The efficient reaction between MTS and E17C suggests that this residue resides in an aqueous environment and is not buried in the membrane.
source: Although approximations of P2X receptor channels in the membrane by databases such as OPM suggest that much of the lateral fenestrations are buried in the membrane (Figure 1), the efficient reaction between MTS and E17C (Figure 5) suggests that this residue resides in an aqueous environment and is not buried in the membrane, supporting its location within the ion permeation pathway at the intracellular end of the pore.
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion as an inference from the data.

claim: E17C is located within the ion permeation pathway at the intracellular end of the pore.
source: Although approximations of P2X receptor channels in the membrane by databases such as OPM suggest that much of the lateral fenestrations are buried in the membrane (Figure 1), the efficient reaction between MTS and E17C (Figure 5) suggests that this residue resides in an aqueous environment and is not buried in the membrane, supporting its location within the ion permeation pathway at the intracellular end of the pore.
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion as an inference from the data.

claim: Charge-reversing mutations in rP2X2 and mP2X5 clearly alter the relative permeability of the two channels.
source: Importantly, charge-reversing mutations in rP2X2 and mP2X5 clearly alter the relative permeability of the two channels (Figure 6 and Figure 8).
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion and supported by Figure 6 and Figure 8.

claim: The effect of the E17K mutation in rP2X2 suggests that other determinants contribute to cation selectivity for this subtype.
source: Although the effect of the mutation in rP2X2 is unambiguous (Figure 6), the result also suggests that other determinants contribute to cation selectivity for this subtype (Kawate et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion as an inference from the data.

claim: K17 is a major determinant of anion permeability in mP2X5.
source: In stark contrast, the influence of the mutations in mP2X5 (Figure 8) suggests that K17 is a major determinant of anion permeability in that subtype.
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion as an inference from the data.

claim: Ion permeation occurs through the lateral fenestrations.
source: Viewed collectively, our results support the idea that ion permeation occurs through the lateral fenestrations and that these structural elements play important roles in determining the ion selectivity of P2X receptor channels.
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion as a conclusion from the data.

claim: Lateral fenestrations play important roles in determining the ion selectivity of P2X receptor channels.
source: Viewed collectively, our results support the idea that ion permeation occurs through the lateral fenestrations and that these structural elements play important roles in determining the ion selectivity of P2X receptor channels.
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion as a conclusion from the data.

claim: The cytoplasmic cap is likely a conserved feature of P2X receptor channels.
source: Many residues at critical positions in the cytoplasmic cap are conserved in other P2X receptor subtypes (Figure 2; Figure 2—figure supplement 1), supporting the notion that the cap is a conserved feature of P2X receptor channels.
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion as an inference from the data.

claim: The cap is likely present in P2X2 receptors.
source: Given that the structures of hP2X3Slow where the cap is seen contain three mutations corresponding to residues present in the slowly desensitizing P2X2 receptor, it would seem likely that the cap will also be present in P2X2 receptors.
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion as an inference from the data.

claim: Results with MTS accessibility and ion selectivity experiments in P2X2 are consistent with the structure of P2X3Slow containing the cytoplasmic cap.
source: Our results with MTS accessibility and ion selectivity experiments in P2X2 are consistent with the structure of P2X3Slow containing the cytoplasmic cap (Hausmann et al., 2014; Mansoor et al., 2016), further supporting the presence of a cap in P2X2 receptors.
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion as an inference from the data.

claim: The critical influence of K17 in P2X5 on ion selectivity would be consistent with the presence of cytoplasmic cap and lateral fenestrations like those present in the P2X3Slow structure.
source: Similarly, the critical influence of K17 in P2X5 on ion selectivity in that subtype would be consistent with the presence of cytoplasmic cap and lateral fenestrations like those present in the P2X3Slow structure.
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion as an inference from the data.

claim: Earlier studies had implicated residues in the outer pore as critical determinants of Ca2+ permeability in P2X receptors.
source: Although earlier studies had implicated residues in the outer pore as critical determinants of Ca2+ permeability in P2X receptors (Migita et al., 2001; Samways and Egan, 2007; Samways et al., 2014), a recent study also implicated residues in the N-terminus of rP2X7 as determinants of Ca2+ permeability (Liang et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion and supported by citations.

claim: A recent study implicated residues in the N-terminus of rP2X7 as determinants of Ca2+ permeability.
source: Although earlier studies had implicated residues in the outer pore as critical determinants of Ca2+ permeability in P2X receptors (Migita et al., 2001; Samways and Egan, 2007; Samways et al., 2014), a recent study also implicated residues in the N-terminus of rP2X7 as determinants of Ca2+ permeability (Liang et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: The E17A mutation in rP2X2 and the equivalent E14A mutation in rP2X7 both diminish fractional Ca2+ current.
source: Indeed, the E17A mutation in rP2X2 and the equivalent E14A mutation in rP2X7 both diminish fractional Ca2+ current (Liang et al., 2019), supporting a role of the lateral fenestrations in ion permeation and selectivity.
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: The E17A mutation in rP2X2 and the equivalent E14A mutation in rP2X7 support a role of the lateral fenestrations in ion permeation and selectivity.
source: Indeed, the E17A mutation in rP2X2 and the equivalent E14A mutation in rP2X7 both diminish fractional Ca2+ current (Liang et al., 2019), supporting a role of the lateral fenestrations in ion permeation and selectivity.
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion as an inference from cited data.

claim: The lateral fenestrations present on both sides of the membrane in structures of P2X receptor channels with ATP bound are continuous and present throughout the region likely spanning the lipid membrane.
source: One of the unique features seen in structures of detergent-solubilized P2X receptor channels with ATP bound is that the lateral fenestrations present on both sides of the membrane, which enable ions to enter or exit the pore (Kawate et al., 2011), are continuous and present throughout the region likely spanning the lipid membrane (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion and supported by Figure 1A and B.

claim: The TM helices in P2X receptors lack intersubunit interactions within the membrane.
source: As a result, the TM helices lack intersubunit interactions within the membrane and all intersubunit interactions occur within the large extracellular domain and within the cytoplasmic cap.
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion as an inference from structural data.

claim: All intersubunit interactions in P2X receptors occur within the large extracellular domain and within the cytoplasmic cap.
source: As a result, the TM helices lack intersubunit interactions within the membrane and all intersubunit interactions occur within the large extracellular domain and within the cytoplasmic cap.
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion as an inference from structural data.

claim: Related membrane-embedded fenestrations have not been observed in structures of other trimeric ion channels under conditions where the open state predominates.
source: Related membrane-embedded fenestrations have thus far not been observed in structures of other trimeric ion channels under conditions where the open state predominates, including acid-sensing ion channels (Jasti et al., 2007; Gonzales et al., 2009; Baconguis et al., 2014; Yoder et al., 2018; Yoder and Gouaux, 2020), epithelial sodium channels (Noreng et al., 2018; Noreng et al., 2020) or proton-activated chloride channels (Ruan et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion and supported by citations.

claim: P2X5 is thought to be widely expressed within neurons in the central nervous system.
source: P2X5 is thought to be widely expressed within neurons in the central nervous system (Guo et al., 2008) as well as in cardiac and skeletal muscle (Garcia-Guzman et al., 1996; Ryten et al., 2001), yet what roles this channel plays will require further investigation.
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion and supported by citations.

claim: P2X5 is expressed in cardiac and skeletal muscle.
source: P2X5 is thought to be widely expressed within neurons in the central nervous system (Guo et al., 2008) as well as in cardiac and skeletal muscle (Garcia-Guzman et al., 1996; Ryten et al., 2001), yet what roles this channel plays will require further investigation.
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion and supported by citations.

claim: The unique ion selectivity of P2X5 receptors is determined by one critical residue within the lateral fenestrations.
source: The unique ion selectivity of P2X5 receptors, determined by one critical residue within the lateral fenestrations, suggests that it may play very different roles than other P2X receptor subtypes.
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion as a conclusion from the data.

claim: P2X5 may play very different roles than other P2X receptor subtypes.
source: The unique ion selectivity of P2X5 receptors, determined by one critical residue within the lateral fenestrations, suggests that it may play very different roles than other P2X receptor subtypes.
evidence: This is stated directly in the discussion as speculation based on the data.
